title: Four Real OA Papers
relevance: SDE OAs hide tests and punish misread definitions, naive algorithms that ignore bounds, and unresolved ambiguous wording—skills these four papers train directly.
company_notes: Flipkart HirePro paper (coding + SQL) transcribed from OA photos; DE Shaw, Millennium, and Uber coding sets formalized from post-test recall with [recon]/[assumed] flags.

phases.goal: Establish the platform constraints and the recurring OA failure modes these papers illustrate.

must_hit.point: On Flipkart HirePro the editor gives a fixed function signature plus a main that does all I/O; you only fill the WRITE YOUR CODE HERE body and cannot see the test cases.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions fixed signature, harness-owned main/I/O, invisible cases, and filling only the stub body.

must_hit.point: HirePro warns not to print arbitrary strings because they contribute to output and fail tests—so no debug cout may survive a submission.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes the no-arbitrary-strings warning and ties it to why blind debugging is hard.

must_hit.point: Golden price means digitSum(G) - maxDigit(G) equals maxDigit(G), equivalently digitSum(G) equals 2 * maxDigit(G), matching samples like 352 and 11.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the rewritten equality and checks 352 (sum 10, max 5) or 11 (sum 2, max 1).

must_hit.point: When a worked explanation's intermediate arithmetic disagrees with the stated rule, trust the rule plus the sample output—not the explanation's intermediates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites Flipkart logistics weather score: explanation says 5 while summing valid R1 alerts yields 8, yet both clear >= 4 so sample outputs still match the rule.

probes: What does the HirePro harness force you to do and forbid, and how do you correctly parse the golden-price definition from the prose?

hints.1: Start from the editor/stub shape and the no-debug-print warning.
hints.2: Rewrite the golden-price sentence as an equality on digit sum and max digit, then check a sample.
hints.3: Say: fixed signature + harness I/O, no surviving cout; digitSum == 2 * maxDigit; if explanation and rule conflict, implement the rule and match sample output.

phases.goal: Show the reframes and algorithms that solve the papers' core problems once the statement is parsed.

must_hit.point: Marathon checkpoints need no tree build: each path string is the node's address, and a node is faulty iff both path+L and path+R exist in the set.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes hashing paths, empty path for the start, and summing nodes with both children present.

must_hit.point: DE Shaw music-player move-before plus positional query fights itself: vector is slow on moves, list is slow on index lookup, so an order-statistic structure (or sqrt buckets) is required at assumed n,q up to 2 * 10^5.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the opposite costs of vector vs list+iterator map and says the intended fix is order-statistic / sqrt decomposition / implicit treap.

must_hit.point: Maximum flips with positive prefixes uses optimistic flips into a max-heap and retracts the largest flipped magnitude when the running sum is no longer strictly positive.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes flip-all-then-unflip-largest (add back 2*x) until every prefix stays > 0, same regret shape as IPO / Course Schedule III.

must_hit.point: Checkerboard subgrids become constant-value rectangles after b[i][j] = g[i][j] XOR ((i+j) & 1), then counted with a histogram/monotonic-stack sweep in O(n*m).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the XOR parity transform and that a rectangle is checkerboard iff b is constant on it; mentions the stack sweep.

must_hit.point: With revisits allowed, shortest start-to-end walk covering k task nodes collapses to BFS distances among k+2 milestones plus bitmask DP; assumed k <= 15 makes the exponential factor intended.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says concatenate shortest paths between milestones, then dp[mask][i] over task subsets; notes unit weights mean BFS not Dijkstra.

must_hit.point: Append-and-reverse is a content-independent position permutation: final b reads same-parity-as-(n-1) indices descending then the other parity ascending, so max b is all 1s then all 0s and s is the inverse perm.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the parity split formula, that characters do not affect landing spots, and recovering s by inverting the permutation onto 1s-then-0s.

must_hit.point: SQL 'not provided' means NULL, empty string, or only blank spaces—so use IS NULL OR TRIM(col) = '' on ContactNumber and Email, with EXISTS for at least one appointment.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions TRIM for blanks, separate IS NULL because TRIM(NULL) is unknown, and EXISTS (or IN/GROUP BY) to avoid duplicating patients.

probes: Pick Marathon checkpoints or the music-player queries and explain the intended structure without implementing the naive story.
How do the max-flips heap, checkerboard XOR, or task-node bitmask DP each follow from one load-bearing clause in the statement?

hints.1: Name the reframing first (addresses / tension / optimistic regret / XOR / milestones / fixed perm / TRIM+EXISTS).
hints.2: For each, say which naive structure fails and what replaces it.
hints.3: Hit: path set + both children; order-statistic vs vector/list; heap retract largest; XOR then histogram count; BFS matrix + bitmask DP for small k; parity perm then invert; IS NULL OR TRIM with EXISTS.

phases.goal: Contrast solution choices these papers force once constraints and wording are fixed.

must_hit.point: Music player: sqrt-bucket decomposition is the OA engineering choice (~passes, short) while an implicit treap is asymptotically better but needs parent pointers for value-to-position and far more code.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares vector TLE, list TLE, bucket O(sqrt) amortized pass, treap O(log) optimal but longer and easier to get wrong.

must_hit.point: Task-cover walk: milestone BFS + bitmask DP fits large n with small k; BFS over (node, mask) is shorter code but needs memory on the order of n * 2^k, which fails at assumed n = 10^5 with k = 15.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both methods and that the constraint on n vs k picks between them.

must_hit.point: Uber duplicate/segment penalty: pair-based reading collapses to sum of min(D,Seg) over equal boundaries; element/run-based reading needs partition DP—and a large n bound retroactively selects the greedy reading.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes Reading A O(n) greedy from Reading B non-linear run cost needing DP; notes candidate's partition-DP instinct and that n at 10^5 would kill O(n^2).

probes: When would you ship sqrt buckets versus an implicit treap for the playlist, or milestone DP versus state-space BFS for the task walk?
How does the penalty-rule reading and the n bound jointly decide greedy versus partition DP?

hints.1: Compare what each approach optimizes and what it spends.
hints.2: Bring in code length, asymptotics, and which constraint breaks which method.
hints.3: Say: sqrt for OA speed/simplicity vs treap for log; DP when n large/k small vs (node,mask) BFS when n small; pair greedy if n is huge, run DP if n is small / statement expects partition DP.

phases.goal: Apply the papers' meta-lessons under blind OA conditions before trusting hand-written examples.

must_hit.point: DE Shaw / Millennium style: the statement literally describes a hopeless naive method; reading the constraint bound first is what reveals order-statistic structures, one-pass heap greedy, linear-ish DP, or intended bitmask exponential.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives at least one pair: sounds like list edits / 2^n subsets / (nm)^2 rectangles / O(n^2) reverse-sim, but bounds demand the advanced reading.

must_hit.point: Logistics Q4 is fidelity under volume: index tables, filter per-shipment facts, then per-route aggregates, then score/filter/sort—scoring in one pass over input is the usual loss.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the fixed dependency order and that route average delay needs every shipment's delay count first, including delivered ones.

must_hit.point: Ambiguous OA phrases (same as its adjacent; flip any consecutive subset) should be resolved by enumerating readings and preferring the clean structure—formula, contiguous feasible range, or separable greedy—not by guessing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Uber Q1 pair vs run and Q3 at-most-once complement giving 1 + n(n+1)/2 independent of content.

must_hit.point: Hand-derived expected answers are unreliable: cross-checks caught wrong Flipkart/DE Shaw examples (max flips answer 3 not 2; music-player header/query mismatch), so brute-force oracles beat staring.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites at least one concrete wrong hand example and that on an OA you then 'fix' correct code.

probes: You get a DE Shaw-style statement that sounds like simple array edits plus large bounds—what do you do before typing?
A sample explanation's intermediate disagrees with your implementation but sample output matches—what do you trust, and how do you validate hand examples?

hints.1: Separate 'what the prose narrates' from 'what the bounds allow'.
hints.2: For spec problems, name the dependency order; for ambiguity, name competing readings.
hints.3: Say: bounds pick the algorithm; implement rule+output over explanation arithmetic; validate examples with brute force because hand answers were wrong in these notes.

tradeoffs.topic: vector vs list vs sqrt buckets vs implicit treap (music player)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: vector: O(1) lookup, O(n) move → TLE at large q; list+iterator map: O(1) splice move, O(n) lookup → TLE; sqrt buckets: both ops ~O(sqrt n) amortized, short, passes; implicit treap: O(log n) both ways but needs parent pointers for value→position and much more code—prefer sqrt in an OA, mention treap in interview.

tradeoffs.topic: milestone BFS + bitmask DP vs BFS on (node, mask)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Both correct when revisits are allowed. Milestone matrix + dp[mask][i] is O((k+2)(n+m) + 2^k k^2) and fits large n with small k. State-space BFS is less code but O((n+m) 2^k) time/memory—unusable at assumed n = 10^5, k = 15.

tradeoffs.topic: Uber duplicate penalty: per adjacent pair vs per element in a run
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Pair reading: each equal boundary independently pays min(D, Seg)—O(n) greedy. Run/element reading: cost is nonlinear in run length, greedy errs often, need partition DP. Candidate reaching for partition DP plus a small n bound points to the run reading; huge n points back to pairs.

tradeoffs.topic: rule text + sample output vs sample explanation intermediates
tradeoffs.strong_answer: OA explanations are hand prose, not generated from the reference. Flipkart weather: explanation totals 5 but valid R1 alerts sum to 8; implementing the rule still matches both sample outputs because the threshold is >= 4. Ground truth is the rule plus printed samples.

gotchas.trap: Leaving HirePro stub seeds like sum=-1 or final_output="NONE" unchanged when no/empty answer should be 0 or "NA".
gotchas.correction: Overwrite answer variables explicitly; the stub initializer is a decoy—the docstring/spec say return "NA", and a no-faulty-checkpoint case must print 0 not -1.

gotchas.trap: Building Marathon as pointer nodes and missing that VLAs in the harness are a GCC extension, or returning -1 when nothing is faulty.
gotchas.correction: Hash path strings and test path+L / path+R; do not 'fix' the VLA; initialize the sum to 0.

gotchas.trap: Computing routeAverageDelayEventCount after dropping delivered shipments, or inventing ids via defaultdict for invalid X9-style records.
gotchas.correction: Every shipment on the route counts in the average, delivered included; drop records whose shipment/route id does not exist—never create rows for them.

gotchas.trap: SQL: col = '' only, or INNER JOIN Appointments for 'at least one'.
gotchas.correction: Treat NULL, '', and blank-only via IS NULL OR TRIM(col)=''; EXISTS (or IN / GROUP BY) keeps one row per patient; Doctors/Specialization tables are decoys.

gotchas.trap: Using int for DE Shaw flip sums, checkerboard counts, or Uber's 1 + n(n+1)/2 at large n.
gotchas.correction: long long is mandatory: flip running sums reach far past 32-bit; all-checkerboard 2000×2000 is about 4·10^12; multiply n*(n+1) in 64-bit before dividing.

gotchas.trap: Simulating Millennium append-and-reverse with a real reverse each step, or trusting an off-by-one parity formula.
gotchas.correction: Defer reverse with a deque + flipped flag (O(n)); verify closed-form index runs against a brute simulator—wrong second-run start duplicates index 0 for n = 1.

gotchas.trap: Reaching for Dijkstra on unit-weight task graphs, or forbidding revisits when the statement allows them.
gotchas.correction: Unit weights ⇒ BFS; revisit permission is what makes legs independent and the milestone reduction valid—without it the problem is much harder.

gotchas.trap: Assuming Uber 'flip substring' may be applied many times, or that the distinct-count depends on the bits of s.
gotchas.correction: Many flips of single chars yield all 2^n strings (too trivial); at most one complement of a block gives exactly 1 + n(n+1)/2 distinct results, independent of content.
